entry.title: Knowing in Your Bones
entry.summary: In a comment on my last post, my friend Kurt Keefner wonders whether Socrates really should be considered a paradigm of the philosopher, since he never wrote a word - and philosophic arguments can't be properly weighed unless they're written down. It just so happens that this very topic was of great concern to Socrates and his student Plato - there's a reason why Plato wrote dialogues as representations of the true path to philosophical insight. entry.title: Friendship Facets
entry.summary: In my experience, one of the beautiful things about friendship (broadly speaking - I've always liked the fact that the ancient Greek word φιλία covers a very wide range of personal relationships) is that each friend brings out different facets of my personality (sometimes latent facets or even facets I didn’t know I had!). And these facets can be quite particular: for instance, I am a musical person, but different friends of mine might prefer classical, folk, blues, jazz, rock, or pop, all of which appeal to me if the artists are good (as Duke Ellington said, "there are two kinds of music: the good kind and the other kind"!). Some friends might be more spontaneous, more emotionally sensitive, more organized, more philosophical, more creative, more athletic, or what have you - and they might bring out those qualities in myself when we interact or when they inspire me to try new things. This is why there really is an art of friendship and of great conversation. As I turn more and more away from abstractions and universals, I find myself giving ever closer attention to the private, personal, practical, passionate, and particular. This is where life really happens, and where I find the greatest wisdom and joy....

entry.title: Personality Facets
entry.summary: Following up on yesterday's post about facets of personhood, I thought I'd write briefly about the more scientific topic of facets in personality psychology. Although I am far from an expert in this field, longtime readers know that I'm skeptical about the popular Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) and prefer the five-factor "OCEAN" model of personality theory (although the six-factor "HEXACO" model seems quite good, too). The five factors are: Openness to Experience, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism (HEXACO adds a factor for Honesty and Humility)....

entry.title: Facets
entry.summary: Two weeks ago today, some friends and I held a celebration of life at the Denver Botanic Gardens for my dear departed Elisa. I waited quite a while to schedule this gathering because Elisa never liked it when other people held such events too close in time to someone's passing. Everyone I've spoken with since then has commented on how beautiful the gathering was; if you ask me, that's because so many beautiful people were there to remember Elisa....
